headline: How to Catch Up on Homeschool Records in One Evening
sub: Set a timer. Most of this takes under 90 minutes.
items: Minutes 0 to 20: Gather workbooks, receipts and your phone. Sort photos by date, newest first.
Minutes 20 to 40: Write one line per subject per week you can place: date range, subject, how far you got.
Minutes 40 to 60: Add library and calendar entries as reading and co-op days. Mark anything approximate as approximate.
Minutes 60 to 75: Check what your state actually asks for before doing any more than that.
Minutes 75 to 90: Record today's session properly, so tomorrow starts the habit instead of another gap.

headline: Why Homeschool Record Keeping Stalls: Habits to Stop
sub: Every one of these feels reasonable in September.
items: Writing it from memory at the end of the week, instead of right after the lesson.
Keeping it somewhere that isn't already open or already in your hand.
Letting one missed day turn into two, then a blank month.
Deciding you'll catch up on it later, which tends to become never.
Waiting for the day to go well before it seems worth writing down.
